title: Tiafoe, Pegula, Fritz among stars confirmed for World Team Tennis return
content:
Taylor Fritz, Frances Tiafoe and Victoria Mboko are among the latest players confirmed for World Team Tennis ahead of its December relaunch, its first season since 2021.

Fritz, the men’s world No. 10, and Tiafoe, No. 12, will join Jessica Pegula and Camila Osorio on the New York Empire Racquet Club, while women’s world No. 15 Mboko, Leylah Fernandez and Gabriel Diallo have been added alongside Denis Shapovalov for the Toronto North Racquet Club. Learner Tien and Iva Jović will play for the Florida Flamingos Racquet Club with Tommy Paul.

WTT, the mixed-gender team tennis league co-founded in the 1970s by 12-time Grand Slam singles champion Billie Jean King, is returning for its 47th season, ending a five-year hiatus. The three-team competition will run from Dec. 1 to Dec. 15, during the offseason for the men’s and women’s tours, with six matches across New York, Toronto and Florida.

“In line with WTT’s original vision, we wanted to have top-ranked players competing against one another in a team setting,” WTT chief executive Stephen Amritraj said. “In one night, fans get to watch elite men and women compete across singles and mixed doubles while representing their teams and cities. It’s more variety, more competition and more meaningful tennis packed into each match.”

Each match will consist of four singles sets, two women’s and two men’s, followed by a mixed-doubles 10-point tiebreak. Each club will start two women and two men, with further player additions expected before the season begins.

New York will host Florida at Barclays Center on Dec. 1 before Toronto visits the same venue the following day. Toronto will then host New York and Florida at Coca-Cola Coliseum on Dec. 5 and 6.

Florida will host the final two matches at Amerant Bank Arena near Miami, facing Toronto on Dec. 14 and New York on Dec. 15. Tickets are expected to go on sale Sept. 15.

The original WTT ran from 1974 to 1978 and featured leading players, including King, Chris Evert, Björn Borg, Rod Laver and Martina Navratilova. Several versions of the league have followed.

The league announced its latest reboot in May, with new ownership through a holding company founded by Amritraj. Pegula was among the first players confirmed to participate.

Organizers have said players will receive ownership stakes in the league alongside base fees and win bonuses.
